title: Best Device Fingerprinting Tools Compared
metaDescription: Tor Browser, Brave, CanvasBlocker, Firefox with uBlock Origin and Incognito Browser (which we make) scored on the same six fingerprinting defences.
intro: Device fingerprinting lets websites track you even after clearing cookies by collecting unique browser and device characteristics. This page scores five browsers and add-ons on six fingerprinting defences, and each rating is worked out from the table.

products.name: Incognito Browser
products.tagline: Android browser that stays in private mode and wipes history, cookies and sessions when you exit
pros: Every tab is private; history, cookies and sessions are wiped when you exit
Settings to switch JavaScript, images and cookies off
Agent Cloaking can mask the browser and device a site sees
cons: Android only: there is no iOS, desktop or web version
Google Play's Data safety section says it may collect crash logs and diagnostics

products.name: Firefox with uBlock Origin
products.tagline: Open-source browser that blocks known fingerprinting scripts
pros: Enhanced Tracking Protection blocks known fingerprinting scripts
uBlock Origin adds extra fingerprinting filters
cons: Requires manual configuration for best protection

products.name: Tor Browser
products.tagline: Browser that routes traffic through Tor and makes users look alike to resist fingerprinting
pros: Standardizes screen size, fonts and user agent across users
Makes users look identical to trackers
cons: Slower than a regular browser, because traffic passes through three relays

products.name: Brave Browser
pros: Randomizes canvas, WebGL and audio readouts by default
Blocks ads and trackers by default
cons: Cryptocurrency features may not appeal to all users

products.name: CanvasBlocker
products.tagline: Firefox add-on that fakes canvas and other fingerprinting readouts
pros: Also fakes WebGL, audio, DOMRect and TextMetrics readouts

features.name: Canvas Fingerprinting Protection
features.description: Blocks websites from reading unique canvas signatures that identify your device

tor-browser.note: Returns identical canvas for all users

features.name: WebGL Fingerprinting Protection
features.description: Prevents websites from identifying your graphics card and driver information

tor-browser.note: Restricts WebGL and reports standard values

features.name: Audio Fingerprinting Protection
features.description: Blocks websites from using audio context to create unique device signatures

features.name: Font Fingerprinting Protection
features.description: Prevents websites from detecting your installed fonts to create a unique profile

firefox-ublock.note: Some font protection in strict mode

canvas-blocker.note: Fakes TextMetrics and DOMRect readouts that font checks can use

features.name: Screen Resolution Spoofing
features.description: Hides or randomizes your actual screen resolution to prevent identification

features.name: User Agent Randomization
features.description: Changes browser identification strings to prevent consistent tracking

incognito-browser.note: Not documented. Agent Cloaking changes the browser and device a site sees, which is not fingerprint protection

canvas-blocker.note: Navigator protection can change what the browser reports; off by default

verdict.summary: Tor Browser scores highest on these six criteria: rather than hiding each signal, it tries to make every user look the same. Brave and CanvasBlocker tie for second (Brave is listed first alphabetically). Brave randomizes canvas, WebGL and audio readouts by default in an everyday browser; CanvasBlocker adds similar faking to Firefox but takes some configuring. Firefox with uBlock Origin is next: Enhanced Tracking Protection blocks known fingerprinting scripts, but several signals are only partly covered. Incognito Browser, which we make, scores lowest: it documents no fingerprinting protection. Its Agent Cloaking changes the browser and device a site sees, which is not the same thing.

bestFor.reason: Scores highest here; aims to make all users appear identical to trackers
Randomizes canvas, WebGL and audio readouts by default, with no setup
Fakes canvas readouts, and WebGL and audio ones too, in Firefox on desktop and Android
Open source and highly configurable, with uBlock Origin's filter lists on top

pro_tips: Test your fingerprinting protection regularly using tools like AmIUnique.org or the EFF's Cover Your Tracks (formerly Panopticlick) to see how unique your browser appears to websites.

Don't stack several anti-fingerprinting add-ons: overlapping tools can make your browser more unusual, not less. Pick one approach, such as Tor Browser, Brave's defaults or CanvasBlocker in Firefox, and test it.
Clear your browser data regularly and use private browsing modes, but remember that fingerprinting can still track you across sessions.
Consider using different browsers for different activities - a hardened browser for sensitive tasks and a regular one for everyday browsing.
Keep your anti-fingerprinting tools updated as new tracking methods emerge constantly and protection needs to evolve accordingly.

faqs.question: What is device fingerprinting and why should I care?
faqs.answer: Device fingerprinting is a tracking method that identifies you based on your browser and device characteristics like screen resolution, installed fonts, and hardware features. Unlike cookies, it persists even when you clear your browser data and can track you across websites without your knowledge.

faqs.question: How effective are anti-fingerprinting tools?
faqs.answer: No tool stops every technique. On this page Tor Browser scores highest because it makes its users look alike rather than hiding each signal separately; Brave and CanvasBlocker randomize or fake readouts instead. Stacking several anti-fingerprinting add-ons can make a browser more unusual and easier to single out, so pick one approach and check it with a test site such as the EFF's Cover Your Tracks.

faqs.question: Will anti-fingerprinting protection break websites?
faqs.answer: Some websites may experience functionality issues when fingerprinting is blocked, particularly those that use canvas or WebGL for legitimate purposes. Most modern anti-fingerprinting tools try to minimize breakage by allowing necessary functions while blocking tracking attempts.

faqs.question: Can I use anti-fingerprinting tools on mobile devices?
faqs.answer: Yes. Brave and Tor Browser have mobile versions with fingerprinting protection, and Firefox for Android can run uBlock Origin and CanvasBlocker. Mobile browsers typically have fewer settings than desktop versions, though, so protection may be more limited.

faqs.question: Is fingerprinting protection legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, protecting yourself from fingerprinting is legal. In the EU, websites generally need your consent before fingerprinting your device under the ePrivacy rules, and the data a fingerprint produces counts as personal data under the GDPR.
